newsitem.title: USA: U.S. PRUDENTIAL WARNED OF SALES ABUSES IN 1982-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. PRUDENTIAL WARNED OF SALES ABUSES IN 1982-WSJ.

text.p: Prudential Insurance Co of America's internal auditors warned the company's directors about deceptive insurance sales practices as early as 1982, according to a Wall Street Journal report.
The newspaper said New Jersey regulators last year said top officials at the Newark, N.J.-based insurer should have known of the widespread problem as early as 1992.
But the Wall Street Journal said it reviewed hundreds of pages of internal documents that show that board members and top executives were told of the abusive sales practices a decade earlier.
In addition, the newspaper said company officials were warned in several successive years that the problems had not been resolved.
Prudential last year agreed to pay policyholders at least $410 million in a class-action settlement of the deceptive sales practice allegations.

The newspaper said the disclosures could have significant legal implications, noting the attorneys who negotiated the class-action settlement never gained access to the material, although they knew it existed.
The settlement is being appealed by lawyers for policyholders who believe it is too soft on Prudential, the newspaper said.
Prudential was not immediately available for comment on Thursday.

But in a statement issued to the Wall Street Journal on Wednesday, Prudential said that before 1992, "senior management presented summary reports on sales-practices matters to the board's auditing committee from time to time.
"Senior management advised the auditing committee that they were taking steps they believed would address those issues raised.

"The auditing committee acted appropriately based on those reports. In hindsight, corrective actions taken by senior management to address sales-practice problems prior to 1992 were not as effective as they could have been," Prudential told the Wall Street Journal in the statement.
Prudential also told the newspaper that it had apologized to customers, cooperated with investigators and believes that "the remediation program which is currently under way is fair and equitable."
